message.content:
In this repository (/bench/repo), I need to answer a precise question about the backend code:

1. Find every distinct declaration of a method/function named exactly `Close` in the backend code (likely Go, based on typical patterns — check the language actually used). This includes things like `func (x *Foo) Close() error { ... }` or `func (x Foo) Close() { ... }` — i.e., a method named Close on some receiver type, defined anywhere under backend source directories (exclude vendor/third-party dependency directories like vendor/, node_modules/, .git/).

2. For each distinct declaration (grouped by receiver type), determine whether that specific type's `.Close()` method is actually invoked (called, e.g. `x.Close()` or `defer x.Close()`) anywhere in non-test server code (i.e., NOT in _test.go files, NOT in test helper packages, NOT in mock files). List the actual caller file:line for each invoked one.

Please:
- First figure out what "backend" means in this repo's structure (look at top-level directories).
- Use grep/ripgrep to find `func.*Close(` declarations (adjust the exact command to the language used - it might be Go, but verify).
- For each declaration, note the file:line and the receiver type.
- Then grep for `.Close()` call sites across non-test files, and match each call site to which type it's calling on (you may need to trace variable types via short context reads).
- Report back: total count of distinct Close declarations, and for each declaration, whether it is called in non-test server code with the specific caller file:line citations.

Be thorough - use grep with counts first to scope the size of the problem before diving into individual files. If there are many declarations (say more than 15-20), prioritize accuracy over exhaustiveness but try to cover all of them, and clearly state if you had to skip any due to volume.

Report your findings in a structured format: total count, then a list of "Type.Close() - declared at path:line - called at path:line (or 'not called in non-test code' or 'not called anywhere found')".

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Backend structure

This repo is a Go backend (the `usememos/memos` app) with a separate TypeScript frontend under `web/`. Backend Go source lives under: `cmd/`, `internal/`, `server/`, `store/`, and `proto/gen/` (generated gRPC-gateway code). I excluded `web/` (frontend), `vendor/` (none present, module-based via go.mod), and `.git/`.

## Search methodology

- `grep -rn "func.*) Close(" cmd internal server store proto --include="*.go"` to find concrete method declarations (receiver-bound `func (x T) Close(...)`).
- Verified two additional `Close()` occurrences (`store/driver.go:12`, `store/cache/cache.go:31`) are **interface method signatures**, not concrete declarations — excluded from the count per the task's definition ("method/function... on some receiver type").
- Confirmed no standalone `func Close(...)` (non-method) exists.
- Grepped all `.Close()` call sites repo-wide, then filtered out `_test.go` files and test-only packages (`store/test/`, `server/router/api/v1/test/`) to find genuine non-test caller sites, tracing each receiver's static type via surrounding struct/field declarations.

## Results

**Total distinct `Close` declarations found: 8** (6 in non-test files, 2 in a test-helper file)

1. **`(*SSEHub).Close()`** — declared at `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`
   Called at `server/server.go:206` (`s.sseHub.Close()`, inside `Server.closeLongLivedConnections`, invoked from `Server.Shutdown`).

2. **`(*Store).Close() error`** — declared at `store/store.go:72`
   Called at `server/server.go:146` (`if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {`, inside `Server.Shutdown`).
   (Also called at `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:66`, but that's test-helper code, not counted as the qualifying non-test call — the `server/server.go:146` site already satisfies "called in non-test code".)

3. **`(*Cache).Close() error`** (package `store/cache`) — declared at `store/cache/cache.go:187`
   Called 3 times at `store/store.go:74`, `store/store.go:75`, `store/store.go:76` (`s.instanceSettingCache.Close()`, `s.userCache.Close()`, `s.userSettingCache.Close()`, all inside `(*Store).Close`, fields are typed `*cache.Cache`).

4. **`(*MemoFilterTestContext).Close()`** — declared at `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200`
   This is declared in a `_test.go` file itself (a test helper type), so by definition it is not used in non-test server code. **Not called in non-test code** (only called from `_test.go` files, e.g. `store/test/memo_filter_test.go` and `store/test/memo_filter_functions_test.go`, dozens of `tc.Close()`/`defer tc.Close()` sites).

5. **`(*AttachmentFilterTestContext).Close()`** — declared at `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:282`
   Same as above — test-only type. **Not called in non-test code** (only called from `store/test/attachment_filter_test.go`, many `defer tc.Close()` sites).

6. **`(*DB).Close() error`** (package `store/db/sqlite`) — declared at `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`
   Not called directly by concrete type anywhere in non-test code. It's reached only polymorphically: `sqlite.DB` implements the `store.Driver` interface, and `store/store.go:78` calls `return s.driver.Close()` on the interface-typed field. **No direct-type call site found**; invocation happens indirectly via the `Driver` interface dispatch at `store/store.go:78` when the sqlite driver is the active one.

7. **`(*DB).Close() error`** (package `store/db/postgres`) — declared at `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`
   Same situation as sqlite: no direct non-test call on the concrete `postgres.DB` type; reached indirectly via `store/store.go:78` (`s.driver.Close()`) when postgres is the active driver. (Note: `store/db/postgres/user_setting_test.go` has direct `db.Close()` calls, but those are test files.)

8. **`(*DB).Close() error`** (package `store/db/mysql`) — declared at `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`
   Same situation: no direct non-test call on the concrete `mysql.DB` type; reached indirectly via `store/store.go:78` (`s.driver.Close()`) when mysql is the active driver.

## Notes / caveats

- Entries 6–8 (`sqlite.DB`, `postgres.DB`, `mysql.DB`) all satisfy `store.Driver` (interface defined at `store/driver.go:9-12`, which itself declares `Close() error` as a requirement, not an implementation). The `Store` type holds a `driver Driver` field and calls `s.driver.Close()` at `store/store.go:78`. This is a genuine runtime invocation of whichever concrete `DB.Close()` is active, but it's a call through an interface variable, not a syntactically type-resolved call — flagging this distinction since the task asked to trace variable types precisely.
- `sql.Rows.Close()` / `sql.DB.Close()` (standard library, e.g. `defer rows.Close()`, `d.db.Close()`) and `net.Listener.Close()`, `http.Server.Close()`, `io.ReadCloser.Body.Close()` etc. appear very frequently throughout `store/db/*` and `server/`, but these are calls on standard-library types, not on any of the 8 locally-declared `Close` methods, so they were excluded from the "declaration" count and are not part of the call-site matching (they're not receivers of our locally defined `Close` methods).
- No declarations or call sites were skipped due to volume — the declaration set was small (8 total) and fully covered.
